overview: This file consists of a Department of State list of papers concerning Japanese communications and transportation, chiefly a 1937 exchange about Japanese telecommunications legislation. It records Ambassador Joseph C. Grew’s submission of a list of laws and regulations effective January 1, 1937; consultation with the Federal Communications Commission over which texts required translation; the Embassy’s later transmission of translations of telegraph and wireless laws governing foreign telegrams, international radiotelegrams, and foreign warships; and the distribution of those materials to the Navy, Commerce, and Federal Communications Commission. The list also notes a separate report from Tokyo by Cameron on Japan’s international telecommunications.

subfiles.title: List of papers on communications and transportation in Japan
subfiles.about: An administrative index summarizes diplomatic and interdepartmental papers concerning Japanese telecommunications laws and international communications.
subfiles.summary: The list traces correspondence beginning with Ambassador Grew’s February 3, 1937 submission of Japanese communications laws and regulations in force on January 1, 1937. It records consultation with the Federal Communications Commission about translation requirements and a reminder that the Embassy had previously supplied translations of Japanese communications laws. A May 5 despatch transmitted translations of major telegraph and wireless measures, which were circulated on June 13 to the Navy Department, Federal Communications Commission, and Department of Commerce; the final entry notes Cameron’s report from Tokyo on Japan’s international telecommunications.

interest: The list provides a compact reconstruction of how Japanese telecommunications law was collected, selected for translation, and circulated within the U.S. government. It is particularly useful for tracing cooperation among the Tokyo Embassy, State Department, Federal Communications Commission, Navy Department, and Commerce Department, as well as American interest in rules affecting foreign messages and warships in Japanese waters. Because this surviving page is an index rather than the referenced papers themselves, it also supplies valuable document numbers, dates, and descriptions for locating the underlying despatches and enclosures.
